Lauren — thanks for the redline. I reviewed with Apex's GC. A few items from our side: 

1) Governing law/venue: Apex prefers New York law and exclusive NY courts for all disputes. They are not comfortable with CA law as a default.

2) Arbitration threshold: Apex is open to arbitration for smaller commercial claims but wants the threshold higher (suggest $100k) and prefers AAA (New York) as the forum due to existing master agreements.

3) Injunctive relief carveout: Apex will agree to a limited carveout for emergency injunctive relief, but they want the clause to require notice and an expedited meet-and-confer with GC representatives before pursuing immediate relief in a court.

We can live with Redwood's injunctive carveout if you accept NY law for the contract and confine Calif. venue to Redwood-only claims (i.e., Redwood may pursue injunctive relief in CA courts when Redwood seeks to protect its IP). Alternatively, consider a neutral law clause (e.g., Delaware) to bridge positions. 

Proposed compromise: Delaware governing law; AAA arbitration (New York) for monetary claims above $75k; explicit, limited carveout for emergency equitable relief for either party to file in a court of competent jurisdiction with immediate notice to the other party.

If Redwood accepts the Delaware + AAA compromise we can close quickly.
